prompt:
Use case: component assembly illustration. Create a clear design sheet showing how the twin-drill vehicle becomes the TWO LOWER-LEG AND FOOT EXTERNAL MODULES of Social Brave King. Ivory landscape background, clean KINETIC_CEL ink/cel style, restrained orange connection arrows, no words. Image 1 is the closed vehicle master; image 2 the authoritative combined robot; image 3 its selected side leg design; image 4 the COMPLETE humanoid core that must keep both its own legs.

Layout three readable panels, no dense engineering schematic. LEFT panel: the current whole twin-drill vehicle in modest front-side view, with its central longitudinal joining seam visible; beneath it show the TWO matching left/right halves slightly separated along that seam. Every half retains one drill, its track/armor module and rear end shell. No extra drills or third module. Show only enough extra pose to communicate the split, not a pile of duplicated tanks.

MIDDLE panel: one separated half reoriented as an UPRIGHT SHIN module next to a faint gray complete core lower leg. The thick white/orange shin armor opens around the EXISTING leg; its black track running gear remains on the outer/front/rear calf perimeter. The ONE silver drill moves on its orange pivot to the UPPER FRONT KNEE location and points horizontally FORWARD, not upward or backward. The module's thick rear chassis end unfolds at the bottom into the orange/ivory FOOT/HEEL external armor around the existing core foot. Indicate the rotation and fitting with a few large arrows and hinge rings; no precise transformation simulation. Keep the ankle joint clear, tread loops mechanically continuous, no detached dangling small track.

RIGHT panel: installed paired legs from hips to feet, same proportions and appearance as image 2, no robot upper body. Ivory core thighs are retained, distinct knees with silver drills pointing forward along each leg's own toe direction, white segmented shin plates in orange supports, broad black front and rear track runs with dark wheels, separate articulated ankles, heavy ivory/orange toe and heel armor. Side/back construction echoes image 3: the front track edge must not disappear behind a blank white plate, the rear track returns around understandable wheel arcs. Both legs use the same module system, not different armor. Faint gray inner-leg structure may peek through at hinge gaps but do not show extra human limbs or make the core vanish. Distinguish core body from vehicle shell in the assembly panel, keep approved final leg shapes in the installed panel. No arbitrary tank turret, train windows, aircraft wings or new fifth component.
